title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 worked example: daily for 10 occurrences

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.quote: Daily for 10 occurrences: ... ==> (1997 9:00 AM EDT) September 2-11

expect.note: DTSTART is synchronised with the rule and is the first instance; COUNT includes it.

rationale: The corpus's control vector: if an engine fails this, nothing else it reports is interpretable.

title: COUNT includes DTSTART when DTSTART matches the rule

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: The COUNT rule part defines the number of occurrences at which to range-bound the recurrence.

normative.title: RFC 8984 §4.3.3 (JSCalendar RecurrenceRule)
normative.quote: the start date-time ... is always the first occurrence in the expansion
normative.note: JSCalendar legislates what RFC 5545 leaves to inference

rationale: Isolates the 'does COUNT count DTSTART' question from every other variable.

title: DTSTART unsynchronised with the rule (the RFC calls this undefined)

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.quote: If the specified recurrence rule does not include the start date-time, then the recurrence instances ... are undefined.

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 5920 (REJECTED, §3.8.5.3 Friday-the-13th example)
normative.note: REJECTED, on the ground that 'the original example intentionally demonstrates the EXDATE feature by excluding the first occurrence' — which presupposes DTSTART *is* emitted. The RFC Editor thereby endorsed the emit reading inside an errata rejection note, which has no normative standing.

normative.title: RFC 8984 §4.3.3 (JSCalendar RecurrenceRule)
normative.quote: the start date-time ... is always the first occurrence in the expansion ... even if it would normally not match the rule

cases.label: emit-dtstart
cases.note: DTSTART is emitted as instance 1 even though 1997-09-02 is a Tuesday and not the 13th. This is JSCalendar's legislated behaviour and the reading the RFC's own Friday-the-13th example (which EXDATEs DTSTART away) presupposes.

cases.label: rule-only
cases.note: DTSTART is a seed only; the set contains rule matches at or after it. python-dateutil, rrule.js and most engines behave this way.

cases.label: reject
cases.note: Refuse the rule as undefined per the literal text of §3.8.5.3.

expect.note: Three readings, one of which the RFC's own example depends on and another of which it declares undefined.

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (BYDAY,BYMONTHDAY)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (BYDAY,BYMONTHDAY)

rationale: DTSTART's role is the deepest under-specification in RFC 5545. §3.8.5.3 says the case is undefined; the same section prints an example that only works if DTSTART is emitted; erratum 5920's rejection entrenches the contradiction; RFC 8984 fixes it in the opposite direction to the ecosystem. Manufacturing a single answer here would be dishonest.

title: RFC 5545's Friday-the-13th example verbatim, with its EXDATE

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.quote: Every Friday the 13th, forever: ... ==> (1998 9:00 AM EST) February 13;March 13;November 13 (1999 9:00 AM EDT) August 13 (2000 9:00 AM EDT) October 13

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 5920 (REJECTED, §3.8.5.3 Friday-the-13th example)
normative.note: a proposal to delete this EXDATE was rejected

expect.note: Under either DTSTART reading the EXDATE removes the 1997-09-02 seed, so this vector is decidable where RRULE-CORE-003 is not.

rationale: Deliberately paired with CORE-003: the same rule becomes NORMATIVE once the EXDATE removes the contested instance. The pair localises the ambiguity precisely.

title: UNTIL is inclusive when it names an instance exactly

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: If the value specified by UNTIL is synchronized with the specified recurrence, this DATE or DATE-TIME becomes the last instance of the recurrence.

expect.note: 1997-09-04T09:00 EDT is 13:00Z, exactly UNTIL, and is therefore included.

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

rationale: Inclusivity is stated normatively and is still implemented as exclusive by some engines; it is cheap to test and decisive.

title: UNTIL one second before an instance excludes it

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

rationale: The exclusive half of the UNTIL boundary; the pair pins the comparison operator exactly.

title: UNTIL must be UTC when DTSTART carries a TZID (erratum 3883's example, corrected)

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: if the 'DTSTART' property is specified as a date with local time and time zone reference, then the UNTIL rule part MUST be specified as a date with UTC time

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 3883 (Verified, Technical, §3.8.5.3 UNTIL example)
normative.quote: UNTIL=19970902T170000Z terminates at 1:00 PM EDT, not 5:00 PM; the correct value is UNTIL=19970902T210000Z

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

rationale: The RFC's own authors got this wrong in a printed example, and two further errata (5872, 6212) are readers getting it wrong in the opposite direction. One correct and two incorrect errata against UNTIL-in-UTC examples is direct evidence that the local-time/UTC boundary is a comprehension trap.

title: The uncorrected erratum-3883 example (UNTIL=...T170000Z)

expect.note: 17:00Z is 13:00 EDT, so only 09:00 and 12:00 local are in range — the behaviour the erratum exists to explain.

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

rationale: Paired with CORE-007 so an engine that silently reads UNTIL as local time is caught: it would emit five instances here instead of two.

title: UNTIL with a floating DTSTART must be floating

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: if the 'DTSTART' property is specified as a date with local time, then the UNTIL rule part MUST also be specified as a date with local time

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

rationale: The floating branch of the UNTIL value-type coupling; engines that normalise everything to UTC internally get this wrong.

title: UNTIL value type mismatched with DTSTART (Z on a floating start)

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: The value of the UNTIL rule part MUST have the same value type as the 'DTSTART' property.

expect.note: MUST-level requirement. Engines that coerce silently produce a set the author did not write.

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

php-rrule@tz2026a.error: InvalidArgumentException: Invalid UNTIL property: if the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with local time, then the UNTIL rule part MUST also be specified as a date with local time

python-dateutil@tz2026a.error: ValueError: RRULE UNTIL values must be specified in UTC when DTSTART is timezone-aware

python-dateutil@tz2026c.error: ValueError: RRULE UNTIL values must be specified in UTC when DTSTART is timezone-aware

rationale: A MUST that the ABNF cannot enforce, so it is hand-checked or not checked at all.

title: COUNT and UNTIL in the same RRULE (forbidden)

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: The UNTIL rule part and the COUNT rule part MUST NOT occur in the same 'recur'.
normative.note: stated only in an ABNF comment, which no generated parser can enforce

normative.title: python-dateutil rrule documentation (until+count deprecation)
normative.note: python-dateutil deprecated accepting both 'to make sure dateutil is fully compliant with RFC-5545'

expect.note: MUST NOT. Admissible non-conformant behaviours observed in the wild: apply whichever bound is hit first; ignore UNTIL; ignore COUNT; emit a deprecation warning and proceed. All are failures against this vector.

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

php-rrule@tz2026a.error: InvalidArgumentException: The UNTIL or COUNT rule parts MUST NOT occur in the same rule

rationale: The only MUST NOT in §3.3.10 expressed exclusively as an ABNF comment. It is the clearest example of a constraint the grammar cannot carry, and therefore of why a conformance corpus is needed at all.

title: INTERVAL counts periods from DTSTART, not from the calendar

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.8.5.3 (Recurrence Rule)
normative.quote: Every 10 days, 5 occurrences: ... ==> (1997 9:00 AM EDT) September 2,12,22;October 2,12

rationale: The direct counterpart of CRON-ANCH-004: RRULE's INTERVAL is anchored to DTSTART and crosses month boundaries; cron's step is anchored to the field's low bound and resets. The two vectors together define the gap any unified model must bridge.

title: Infinite recurrence with no COUNT and no UNTIL

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: If neither the COUNT nor UNTIL rule parts are present, the recurrence rule is considered to repeat forever.

cases.label: lazy-iterator
cases.note: The engine returns a lazy sequence and the caller takes 5. The only behaviour that composes with a scheduler.

cases.label: caller-bounded
cases.note: The engine requires an explicit window and returns the same prefix.

cases.label: materialise
cases.note: Engines whose only API materialises the whole set hang or exhaust memory. Recorded as a result, not excused.

expect.note: 'Repeats forever' is normative; what an API does with it is not.

rationale: RFC 5545 places no bound on expansion cost. Every practical engine must therefore add a policy the standard does not define, and the corpus records which one.

title: Bounded-range query over an infinite rule (between semantics)

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.note: the RFC defines a recurrence *set*; it defines no range query, so endpoint inclusivity is entirely a library invention

cases.label: half-open
cases.note: The convention most range APIs use elsewhere in the same codebases.

expect.note: Three inclusivity conventions ship, and one library (dateutil) defaults to the rarest of them.

rationale: Range queries are how every scheduler actually consumes a recurrence, and the endpoints are exactly where double-firing and missed-firing bugs live. The RFC is silent, so this is POLICY_DEPENDENT by construction.

title: FREQ missing

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: The FREQ rule part ... This rule part MUST be specified in the recurrence rule.

python-dateutil@tz2026c.error: TypeError: rrule.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'freq'

title: INTERVAL=0

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: The INTERVAL rule part ... contains a positive integer representing at which intervals the recurrence rule repeats.

expect.note: Observed failure modes include an infinite loop and a silent coercion to 1.

ice_cube@tz2026a.error: ArgumentError: '0' is not a valid input for interval. Please pass a postive integer.

pandas@tz2026a.error: ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero

pandas@tz2026c.error: ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero

php-rrule@tz2026a.error: InvalidArgumentException: The INTERVAL rule part must be a positive integer (> 0)

rationale: A crash-class vector on a MUST-shaped word ('positive').

title: COUNT=0

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: COUNT ... defines the number of occurrences at which to range-bound the recurrence
normative.note: the ABNF is 1*DIGIT, which admits 0; the prose does not say whether 0 is legal

cases.label: dtstart-only
cases.note: Engines that always emit DTSTART first and then apply COUNT.

php-rrule@tz2026a.error: InvalidArgumentException: COUNT must be a positive integer (> 0)

rationale: The ABNF admits a value the prose never contemplates; three behaviours ship.

title: UNTIL earlier than DTSTART (empty recurrence set)

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.note: no statement about an UNTIL that precedes DTSTART

cases.label: empty
cases.note: The set is empty; the caller sees no occurrences.

cases.label: dtstart-only
cases.note: Engines that emit DTSTART unconditionally before applying UNTIL.

expect.note: The empty recurrence set is under-specified identically in both grammars; compare CRON-INV-007.

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (UNTIL)

rationale: Paired deliberately with the cron empty-set vectors. A product that promises 'never silently empty' has to answer this in both grammars with the same policy.
